transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-07-28
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Samira Chen (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Acme CTO), Priya Desai (Acme ML Lead), Marco Ruiz (Acme SRE)
Recording id: ff-20260728-acme-poc-9273

Summary (auto): POC scoping focused on defining latency and throughput SLOs for a 4-week POC. Discussed TTFT vs TPOT, percentile targets (p95/p99), workload sizing (QPS, prompt sizes), benchmarking approach (synthetic vs replay), measurement plan and timeline. Action items and next steps agreed.

Topics: latency SLOs, TTFT vs TPOT, p95/p99 targets, throughput sizing, benchmark methodology, cache warm vs cold, measurement instrumentation, POC timeline

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for carving out the time. quick intros? i'll kick it off — jordan patel, i'm the AE on the account. samira is our se who will lead the benchmark / perf work.
[00:12] Samira (Redwood): hi all, samira chen, hi. i'll mostly be on the technical pieces and the load testing.
[00:18] Liam (Acme): liam here, cto. we'll be bringing priya and marco for the ml and infra details.
[00:24] Priya (Acme): hey, priya desai, ml lead, focused on latency for our chat and code-assist flows.
[00:30] Marco (Acme): marco ruiz, sre. i'll provide qps numbers and help with tracing / network setup.

[00:45] Jordan: goal for today is to lock down success criteria for the poc — specifically latency/throughput slos, what to measure, and a timeline. we also want to outline the benchmark plan. does that match what you expected?
[00:52] Liam: yep that's right. high level — our users expect snappy first responses in the UI, and overall throughput matters since we have bursts.

[01:20] Samira: before we dive in, quick terminology check — we use TTFT (time-to-first-token) which is from request arrival to first token emitted, and TPOT (time-per-output-token or time-to-produce tokens) which is the per-token generation time. we also look at end-to-end response time when you need the full generated sequence. sometimes folks conflate TPOT with TTR but we'll be explicit.

[01:48] Priya: that definition works. for the chat flow, TTFT is most important — first token latency drives perceived snappiness. for longer completions, average TPOT matters.

[02:10] Marco: important to capture p95 and p99 tails — our SLAs are strict around p99 for customer-facing flows.

[02:35] Samira: ok good. recommended baseline targets for small prompts (<128 tokens): TTFT p95 < 400ms, p99 < 900ms; TPOT steady-state ~20-40ms/token depending on model size and quantization. for larger prompts (512 tokens), TTFT p95 < 700ms, p99 < 1.5s — these are starting points; we will tune batching and cache to meet them.

[03:10] Priya: are those numbers machine-checked against a model family? like 7B vs 70B?

[03:20] Samira: good question — yes these are approximate for optimized 7B-13B variants with quantization (e.g., 4-bit) on A100 or H100-class infra. if you want 70B, expect higher TPOT and TTFT. we'll include model variant matrix in the SOW.

[03:55] Liam: our initial plan is to use a 13B optimised model for chat. target baseline traffic is 20 qps sustained, with 200 qps burst capacity during peak.

[04:20] Samira: perfect. so on throughput SLOs, we recommend specifying a steady-state qps that meets latency SLOs (e.g., 20 qps at TTFT p95 < 400ms) and a burst handling capacity (e.g., sustain short bursts up to 200 qps with graceful degradation and fallback to smaller models). the POC will measure both steady-state and ramped bursts.

[04:58] Marco: what about caching? we have a lot of similar prefixes; if kv cache or prefix cache is cold our TTFT will spike. we need tests for warm vs cold caches.

[05:15] Samira: absolutely — measurement plan has distinct phases: cold-start baseline (empty KV cache), warm cache scenario (primed with typical prefixes), and production-replay scenario (replay traces at scaled qps). we'll also do incremental batch size and concurrency sweeps.

[05:42] Jordan: let's talk measurement instrumentation. marco, we need access to either logs or a sample of production traces — request timestamps, prompt lengths, tokens-per-response, and QPS patterns.

[05:58] Marco: i can export traces; i'll anonymize and share a 24-hour slice that shows peak windows.

[06:08] Priya: we will also share a representative prompt set — small chat prompts, medium (200-400 token) completions, and a few long-form tasks.

[06:20] Samira: great. for metrics we'll capture: client-side TTFT and end-to-end latency, server-side ingress->first-token and last-token, per-token throughput, GPU utilization, batch sizes, queue time, and error rates. we'll compute p50/p90/p95/p99 over sliding 5m and 1h windows.

[06:52] Liam: can the redwood console show those percentiles live?

[06:58] Samira: yes, Redwood Console will show per-route percentiles, token counts, and traces. we'll also ship a CSV/TSV export with raw latencies. note: transcription — redwood console sometimes shows product name as rewood-console in logs but that's just the exporter id, minor naming quirk.

[07:25] Marco: timeline — how long for the POC and what are the weekly milestones?

[07:30] Jordan: proposal is a 4-week POC: week 0 (setup & baseline), week 1 (synthetic baselines + cold/warm tests), week 2 (prod replay & tuning), week 3 (final validation, handoff and runbook). we can shift if you need longer for compliance.

[07:58] Priya: sample measurement plan — do you have the load-gen configs? we want to replicate accurately (think: concurrency, open vs closed load, ramp profiles).

[08:10] Samira: yes we'll send the benchmark scripts (k6 + custom loader) and recommended profiles: closed-loop for steady-state (20 qps target), open-loop for bursts (200 qps bursts of 30s with 5x ramp), and replay harness for production traces. we'll include warm-up durations and KV cache priming steps.

[08:44] Liam: how do we measure TPOT precisely? client-side token timestamps are noisy.

[08:51] Samira: two approaches: capture server-side token emit timestamps (best if you can enable the token-level trace flag) and measure at the client by streaming timestamps. we'll correlate both. for p99 per-token, we'll use server-side traces because they are less impacted by network jitter.

[09:12] Marco: any advice on sampling? we can't keep full token traces for all requests due to storage and PII.

[09:20] Samira: sensible defaults — sample 1% of traffic for full token traces, collect headers/latency metadata for 100% of requests. for the POC we can increase sampling to 10% for short windows during the replay tests. all traces will be redacted per your privacy policy.

[09:45] Priya: success criteria proposed from our side: UX metric — TTFT p95 < 400ms for normal chat prompts; reliability — error rate < 0.5% during steady-state; throughput — sustain 20 qps with those latency targets and survive 200 qps bursts with graceful fallback.

[10:05] Jordan: that's consistent with what we proposed. we'll codify exact thresholds in the SOW and instrument automated checks so pass/fail is clear.

[10:18] Samira: additional test cases — cold restart (simulate node replacement), noise tests (background embed/other workloads running), and model variant swap (13B -> 7B fallback). we'll capture how the system routes traffic and latency impacts.

[10:50] Marco: for routing, we need to know how automatic fallback works. can redwood route by policy and keep trace continuity?

[10:58] Samira: yes, smart routing can route to cheaper or smaller model variants based on policy. traces will include model_variant metadata so you can see when fallback happens. small caveat — if a fallback is triggered mid-generation you might see truncated sequences; we will avoid that by preferring fallbacks on new requests or at route-level.

[11:25] Liam: what's the expected measurement noise? like, variability day to day? we want to set realistic windows for p99 measurement.

[11:33] Samira: tails are noisy — p99 can vary with small infra events. we recommend reporting p99 over multiple runs and using the 95th percentile of daily p99s as a robust metric, plus looking at p95 as a stable indicator. also use rolling 1h windows to spot regressions.

[11:58] Priya: will you provide a benchmark report template? we want the same format as your internal perf docs.

[12:04] Samira: yes, we'll provide a report with plots (latency percentiles, qps, batch size histograms, GPU util). expect CSV plus a short slide deck summary.

[12:25] Jordan: let's capture the POC acceptance criteria now so it's explicit. three buckets: performance, reliability, and instrumentation/compliance.
[12:34] Samira: performance: TTFT p95 < 400ms and p99 < 900ms for <128-token prompts under 20 qps steady-state. throughput: sustain 20 qps with <0.5% errors.
[12:48] Samira: reliability: system maintains availability >99.9% for the POC window, fallback behavior documented and tested.
[12:56] Samira: instrumentation/compliance: we can produce audit logs, enable SSO to your test tenant, and share SOC2 docs; security review to be scheduled if needed.

[13:12] Marco: that availability number seems tight for a small POC, but ok if it's just for acceptance. we'll test failover scenarios.

[13:24] Jordan: timeline recap — we'll draft SOW and send to liam by friday (2026-07-30). once SOW accepted, week-of-2026-08-03 we provision the test tenant and run baseline tests. benchmark kickoff meeting proposed 2026-08-04.

[13:44] Priya: any costs we should budget for? dedicated capacity vs hosted?

[13:50] Jordan: POC pricing in the SOW will outline a short-term reserved capacity / trial credits. if you want Dedicated for guaranteed latencies, we can include pricing options; otherwise hosted with burst capacity works for the POC. we'll include both scenarios.

[14:10] Marco: instrumentation detail — include request IDs and tracing headers in responses so our side can correlate.

[14:15] Samira: yes, we'll add a correlation header and share the mapping doc.

[14:30] Priya: one more — how do you measure cold-cache impact?

[14:36] Samira: we do cold-start tests by starting from empty KV cache and measuring initial TTFT trajectories — capture first N requests and plot decay as cache warms. we also simulate node reboots to see cache re-population behavior.

[14:55] Liam: ok, i think we're aligned. let's list meeting deliverables and owners.

[15:03] Jordan: deliverables: SOW + pricing (jordan), benchmark scripts + load profiles (samira), sample traces (marco), prompt set + success criteria confirmation (priya). due dates as discussed.

[15:20] Priya: fine. i'll review the SOW and confirm the prompt set by 2026-07-31.

[15:30] Marco: i'll extract the 24h traces and share by 2026-07-29.

[15:35] Jordan: perfect. any final questions?

[15:40] Liam: just one — if we see we can't meet p99 with 13B, is model fall-back part of the POC?

[15:45] Samira: yes fallback is part of the plan; we'll test 13B -> 7B fallbacks and quantify quality regressions. tradeoffs will be part of the final report.

[15:55] Jordan: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the SOW and calendar invites for the kickoff.

[16:05] End notes (auto): Links referenced during call: SOW template (link sent after call), benchmark scripts repo (to be shared), sample security docs (SOC2 / network diagram).
